module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.Simplex.Basic

public section

namespace Affine.Simplex
variable {k V P : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [AddTorsor V P] [PartialOrder k]
  [ZeroLEOneClass k] {n : ℕ}

@[simp] lemma closedInterior_nonempty (s : Simplex k P n) : s.closedInterior.Nonempty :=
  ⟨_, s.point_mem_closedInterior 0⟩

end Affine.Simplex

findings.description: Lines 26–27 duplicate the imported Mathlib lemma `Affine.Simplex.nonempty_closedInterior`. The assumptions and conclusion are identical, and both proofs use `s.points 0` with `s.point_mem_closedInterior 0`. The only additional behavior is the `[simp]` attribute. This is an API duplication, not a mathematical misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: The checked-out Mathlib file `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/Simplex/Basic.lean`, lines 501–503, already states `lemma nonempty_closedInterior [ZeroLEOneClass k] {n : ℕ} (s : Simplex k P n) : s.closedInterior.Nonempty := ⟨s.points 0, s.point_mem_closedInterior 0⟩`, under the same surrounding assumptions. Lean `#print` confirmed the identical types and proofs.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse `Affine.Simplex.nonempty_closedInterior` and update the two calls in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/633.lean`. If the simplifier behavior is desired, register the existing theorem with `[simp]` rather than reproving it under another name.

status_issues.recorded: `@[category research open]`, with an `answer(sorry)` classification set, in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/633.lean:73–75`.
status_issues.source_status: Solved by Michael Beeson, Miklós Laczkovich, and Yan X. Zhang in `Solution of Erdős Problem 633`, arXiv:2604.03609, first submitted 4 April 2026; the consulted version is v3, dated 25 August 2026. Theorem 1 gives a complete classification.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/633 is marked `SOLVED` and says: “A complete classification is given by Beeson, Laczokovich, and Zhang [BLZ26].” The abstract at https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03609 explicitly says the paper settles problem 633. The downloaded source's Theorem 1 characterizes triangles admitting a non-square tiling by eight cases.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and cite BLZ26. When filling the answer set, use the complement of the eight classes in Theorem 1, since the Lean question asks for triangles admitting only square tilings.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the reviewed file, which contains one proved lemma and no new definitions. `Fin (n + 1)` always contains index 0; in dimension 0 the closed interior is a singleton. Mathlib proves agreement with the usual convex hull over ordered fields. Both direct uses correctly exclude zero-piece triangle decompositions. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` and `/workspace/review/use_sites.lean` compile successfully, checking singleton and one-point-space cases, convex-hull agreement, empty-union exclusion, and the valid one-piece decompositions for both cutting notions. The checked proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. No checkout files were edited.
